basis: Resistance to progesterone action is an endocrine signaling disorder; infertility is its reproductive manifestation.
Inherited degeneration of distal motor neurons or axons; weakness and muscle wasting are consequences of denervation.
EBV-associated NK-cell leukemia/lymphoma; hepatic infiltration and dysfunction occur commonly, in over half of patients.
Immune-mediated pustular skin disease; psoriatic arthritis is separately diagnosed. Oral signs do not establish persistent functional damage; renal involvement is under 30%.
Benign osteogenic tumor arising in bone.
Autoimmune inflammatory myopathy; interstitial lung disease is frequent (30-79%). Cardiac disease is occasional (5-29%).
Glycogen storage disorder with central and peripheral neurodegeneration; bladder dysfunction is neurogenic, without established direct urinary tract damage.
Inherited mitochondrial iron-sulfur transport disorder causing sideroblastic anemia and cerebellar dysfunction; ocular motor findings reflect neurologic disease.
Larval infection with variable neural, ocular or visceral migration; severe CNS disease is prominent clinically, but its frequency across all infection forms is uncertain.
Primary melanoma arising from leptomeningeal melanocytes within the central nervous system.
Congenital absence or hypoplasia of central hand and foot skeletal structures; broader TP63 syndromic features are not established for this subtype.
Cholesterol synthesis defect with profound developmental impairment; optic nerve hypoplasia and skeletal defects each 2/3. Valve defect (1/3) omitted by cap; skin signs lack clear damage.
Intellectual disability defines the umbrella; ocular and skeletal abnormalities vary across subtypes and are not established as common damaging features.
Inherited rod-cone retinal degeneration with visual field constriction and reduced visual acuity.
Progressive retinal degeneration; supplied hearing-loss frequencies conflict with the predominantly nonsyndromic RP umbrella and should not be generalized.
Brain and retinal disease define syndrome; fractures 8/12 and GI vascular lesions with bleeding ~46%. Nail dystrophy and anemia (each 5/13) omitted by cap.
Cataract is an opacity of the ocular lens.
Glycine metabolism/mitochondrial disorder with encephalopathy; apnea is neurologic. Isolated hepatic and cardiac reports do not establish involvement in at least 30%.
Progressive motor neuron disease; dysphagia, impaired mastication and slow saccades reflect neurologic dysfunction rather than direct gut or eye damage.
Limb agenesis defines disease; lung hypoplasia, hydrocephalus and orofacial clefts each 80-99%; anal atresia 30-79%. Renal, ocular, ear and cardiac defects omitted by cap.
Tumor of hormone-producing Leydig cells, the endocrine compartment of the testis; gynecomastia has no organ axis.
Noninfectious inflammation of the meninges; heterogeneous causes do not establish a shared autoimmune or immune-mediated mechanism.
EBV-driven proliferation of B, T or NK lymphocytes, including lymphoma/leukemia; extranodal organs vary across the umbrella.
Inherited atrial cardiac rhythm disorder; thromboembolic complications are risks rather than defining organ involvement.
Carcinoma arising in the duodenum; metastatic sites are not defining or consistently common across the concept.
